validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, distinct transmission gas trunk. THREE independent origins name it by this exact name: (1) Ukrtransgaz's own historical chronology (utg.ua, archived) states '1984 р. Введено в експлуатацію магістральний газопровід Єлець - Курськ – Диканька' (1984: the Yelets-Kursk-Dykanka trunk gas pipeline was put into operation) -- confirms existence + StartYear1=1984 exactly; (2) the Kursk Oblast (Russia) regional government's official infrastructure page (archived) lists it by name among the 5 named threads of the Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod corridor passing through the oblast, giving 'diameter 1220 mm, working pressure 55 kg/cm2, throughput 65 mln.m3/day' -- confirms Diameter=1220mm and Capacity=65 mill.Sm3/day exactly as recorded; (3) Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's own Eletskoe LPUMG operational-unit page (archived) lists 'Elets-Kursk-Dykanka' among the trunk pipelines it keeps in reliable operation ('надежная эксплуатация'), separate from 'Elets-Kursk-Kiev' -- corroborates active/operating status (as of that page's Sept-2023 live-retrieval per the sheet's own citation trail) and independently corroborates existence. All three sources are genuinely independent origins (Ukrainian state gas-transit company, Russian regional government, Gazprom's own regional operating unit) -- tier high for existence/classification/diameter/capacity/start-year. DUPLICATE CHECK: investigated against the near-identical-name P0776 (Yelets-Kursk-Kyiv, 297km/45mmcm/d) and the same-origin P0783 (Yelets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih, 95mmcm/d) and P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod trunk, 1420/1400mm, 32mmcm/d) -- REFUTED. Both the Kursk Oblast source and the Gazprom Eletskoe LPUMG source independently list Yelets-Kursk-Dykanka and Yelets-Kursk-Kyiv as two DISTINCT named lines with different diameters/pressures/capacities in the same paragraph (Dykanka thread: 1220mm/65mmcm/d vs Kyiv thread: 1220mm/45mmcm/d), and the Kursk source's framing (5 named threads making up the multi-line 'Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod' corridor through the oblast) is the same Soviet multi-thread-trunk pattern already established for P3484/P5938 (Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna I/II) -- each physically distinct named pipe legitimately gets its own PID; P0775 is not a subset or relabel of P0768 or P0783. CAVEATS: (a) LENGTH -- 298km could not be independently corroborated from any public source found (energybase.ru, the sheet's primary cited source, returns an access-denial page live and has zero Wayback captures for this URL); it is not contradicted by anything found, so left as-is rather than flagged as a spec concern. (b) STATUS post-Jan-2025 -- the RU-UA transit contract (and the Sudzha entry point this pipeline feeds into) ceased 1 Jan 2025, and a Russian state-media report (RIA Novosti, 21 Aug 2025) on accelerated dismantling of the 'Ukraine project' pipelines specifically named a downstream compressor station (Lubny, Poltava Oblast) on this same Yelets-Dykanka-Kyiv corridor as a recent strike target. Per standing country guidance this is NOT treated as evidence THIS specific line is out of service (no line-specific dated evidence found either way), so Status=operating is left unchanged, but current-year confidence in it is lower than the medium-2023 corroboration suggests. (c) OWNERSHIP structure (Gazprom PJSC 48.60% / Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine, unstated remainder) is structurally consistent with the country-standing rule that Gazprom holds only the Russian-territory share of a cross-border line and the Ukrainian TSO holds the Ukrainian share -- no attribution concern on the split itself, but the exact 48.60% figure could not be independently verified from any public source and is left as-is (not fabricating a confirming ref).

validity.recommendation: update EndPrefecture/District from 'Dykanka Raion' to 'Poltava Raion' -- Dykanka Raion was abolished 18 July 2020 in Ukraine's nationwide raion-consolidation reform and its territory (incl. Dykanka) merged into the enlarged Poltava Raion. EndState/Province ('Poltava Oblast') is unaffected and remains correct.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's row records EndPrefecture/District='Dykanka Raion', but that administrative unit no longer exists: on 18 July 2020 the Verkhovna Rada's nationwide raion reform reduced Poltava Oblast from ~25 raions to 4, and Dykanka Raion's territory was absorbed into Poltava Raion. Confirmed independently on both the English and Ukrainian Wikipedia articles for 'Dykanka Raion' / 'Диканський район' (distinct editorial projects, both citing the underlying Ukrainian legislative act, neither GEM-derived) -- both state the raion was abolished in the 2020 reform. This is a stale pre-2020 administrative label, not a wrong settlement (Dykanka the town/hromada itself is real and correctly the pipeline's endpoint) -- a scoped correction to the district field only.

fills.researcher_notes: Both the Kursk Oblast government infrastructure page and Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's Eletskoe LPUMG page describe 'Elets-Kursk-Dykanka' as one of the region's 'magistral'nye gazoprovody' (trunk gas pipelines) -- confirms Fuel=Gas.
Both sources explicitly classify it as a 'magistral'nyi gazoprovod' (trunk/transmission gas pipeline), matching PipelineType=transmission.

Ukrtransgaz's own historical chronology page states explicitly, under the 1984 entry: 'Введено в експлуатацію магістральний газопровід Єлець - Курськ – Диканька' (the Yelets-Kursk-Dykanka trunk gas pipeline was commissioned). Only one source found stating the exact year (no second independent source located for the year specifically, though existence/name is corroborated by two further sources in the validity entry) -- tier medium.

Kursk Oblast government page: '«Елец-Курск-Диканька» диаметр трубы 1220 мм' -- exact match. Only one source found with a numeric diameter figure (Gazprom's own LPUMG page names the pipeline but does not repeat the spec numbers) -- tier medium.

Same Kursk Oblast government page: '...производительность 65 млн. м3/сут.' (throughput 65 million m3/day) -- exact match to Capacity=65.00 mill.Sm3/day. Single-source numeric confirmation -- tier medium.

All three independent sources name the pipeline by exactly this route ('Yelets - Kursk - Dykanka' / 'Елец-Курск-Диканька' / 'Єлець - Курськ – Диканька'), which by construction confirms StartLocation=Yelets (Lipetsk Oblast, Russia -- Yelets is a well-known Lipetsk Oblast city) and EndLocation=Dykanka (Poltava Oblast, Ukraine). NOTE: see the paired attribution concern above -- EndPrefecture/District='Dykanka Raion' is stale (abolished 2020); StartLocation/StartState/Province/EndLocation/EndState/Province themselves are unaffected and confirmed.

Gazprom Transgaz Moskva's Eletskoe LPUMG page lists 'Elets-Kursk-Dykanka' among the trunk pipelines under its 'reliable operation' (надежная эксплуатация) -- i.e. in service, not decommissioned. The sheet's own gem.wiki citation trail shows this exact URL was checked live as recently as 11 Sept 2023 (predating the 1 Jan 2025 RU-UA transit-contract expiry); the live site is currently unreachable (connection refused) so only the 2017 Wayback capture could be directly re-verified here. CAVEAT: does not by itself establish current (2026) status -- transit through Sudzha (which this line feeds) ceased 1 Jan 2025, and a downstream compressor station on this same corridor (Lubny, Poltava Oblast) was reported as a strike target in Aug 2025 Russian state media. No line-specific dated evidence that P0775 itself is out of service was found, so Status=operating is left unchanged per standing country guidance (transit cessation alone is not grounds to retire a line), but confidence should be treated as lower than the source date suggests.

298 km could not be independently corroborated. The sheet's own primary cited source (energybase.ru/pipeline/yelets-kursk-dikanka) returns a live access-denial page (blocked) and has zero Wayback Machine captures for this URL (confirmed via CDX API). Ukrtransgaz, Kursk Oblast government, and Gazprom Transgaz Moskva sources all name the pipeline but none states its total length. No contradicting figure found either -- left as UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating a ref.

summary: P0775 (Yelets-Kursk-Dykanka) CONFIRMED real and correctly classified via 3 independent sources (Ukrtransgaz, Kursk Oblast RF government, Gazprom Transgaz Moskva), which also refute a plausible duplicate concern vs P0776/P0783/P0768 (distinct named threads, not the same pipe). Diameter/Capacity/StartYear1/Location/Fuel/PipelineType/Status refs added (tiers high/medium); Length stays UNRESOLVED (sheet's own cited source, energybase.ru, is blocked live with zero Wayback captures). One genuine ATTRIBUTION concern flagged: EndPrefecture/District='Dykanka Raion' is a stale pre-2020 unit, abolished 18 Jul 2020 and merged into Poltava Raion.
